evidence.title: Generated reasoning sometimes omits supplied influences
evidence.observation: Anthropic reports that Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 often used supplied hints without acknowledging them in generated reasoning. Outcome-based training improved disclosure initially but plateaued. This demonstrates incomplete disclosure in these constructed tests, not complete access to internal causes.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-009: Paper Figure 1; sections 3–5; section 7.2 and conclusion, printed pp. 2, 12 (PDF pages 2, 12). Companion: Testing for faithfulness; Can we improve faithfulness?; Faithfulness and reward hacking.

evidence.limitations: Hint-based multiple-choice tasks needed little reasoning; disclosure was nonzero in most settings. Authors explicitly retain promise for detecting some unwanted behavior and do not establish failure on tasks requiring extended reasoning or tool use. Absence from a trace cannot establish absence of influence; equally, an omission alone does not establish deliberate concealment.
evidence.open_questions: Generalization to operational traces, contemporary models, rare failures and reasoning-intensive actions is unresolved here.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.

relationships.explanation: Qualifies what the specified evidence or monitoring arrangement can establish.
Qualifies confidence outside the tested conditions; success or failure is not universal.
